title: Chapter 4 Quiz 2
description: Filling an array with a loop and visiting every cell.
topic: Creating and traversing a one-dimensional array
instructions: Chapter 4: Creating and traversing a one-dimensional array.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which loop is the natural choice to visit every cell of an array of 5 cells?
questions.explanation: We know the number of cells, so For is ideal.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that fills an array of 10 averages.
questions.code:
Declare averages [1..10] : ARRAY OF real
Declare i As integer
For i From 1 To 10 Do
    Write('Enter the average of student: ', i)
    Read({{1}})
EndFor
questions.explanation: Each pass reads one value into cell i.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that adds the elements of E[1..5].
questions.code:
Declare sum ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    Read(E[i])
    sum ← {{1}} + E[i]
EndFor
Write('The sum is: ', {{2}})
questions.explanation: The accumulator adds each element, then we show it.

questions.question: E = [3, 8, 2, 7, 5]. What is the sum of the elements?
Trace the sum of E = [4, 6, 1, 9, 5]. Give the sum after each pass.
What is the product of [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]? (start with product ← 1)
questions.explanation: 2 × 3 = 6; × 4 = 24; × 5 = 120; × 6 = 720. Watch out: this is a product, not a sum (which would be 20).

questions.question: Why does the product start at 1 and not 0?
options: The sum must start at 1 too
Zero cannot be stored in memory
questions.explanation: 1 is the neutral element for multiplication. Watch out: a sum starts at 0, but a product starts at 1.

questions.question: Put the steps of the sum algorithm in order.
questions.explanation: Initialize, traverse and add, then display.

questions.question: This algorithm should add the 5 elements of E. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Declare sum As integer
Let sum ← 1
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    sum ← sum + E[i]
EndFor
Display(sum)
questions.explanation: A sum starts at 0. Watch out: starting at E[1] would count the first element twice.

questions.question: This algorithm should add the 5 elements read from the keyboard. One line has an error.
questions.code:
Let sum ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    Read(E[i])
    sum ← sum + E[i + 1]
EndFor
Display(sum)
questions.explanation: We must add the element just read, E[i]. Watch out: E[i + 1] is the next cell, and on the last pass it is outside the array.
